name: Science — Inquiry Investigation
subject: Science & Technology
desc: Structured inquiry lesson using the scientific method. Students form a hypothesis, design a fair test, collect data, and draw conclusions. Adaptable to any science unit.

data.lessonTitle: Scientific Inquiry — Designing a Fair Test
data.achKnowledge: Identify the key components of a fair test: variable, constant, hypothesis, observation.
data.achThinking: Design an investigation that controls variables and collects accurate data.
data.achCommunication: Record observations using scientific vocabulary and communicate findings clearly.
data.achApplication: Connect investigation results to real-world scientific phenomena.
data.assessDiagnostic: Quick-write: "What do scientists do when they want to answer a question about the world?" Discuss as class.
data.assessFormative: Monitor lab notebooks during investigation. Questioning: "What is your variable? How are you keeping things fair?"
data.assessAs: Students peer-review each other's hypothesis and procedure using a structured checklist.
data.assessOf: Lab report: hypothesis, procedure, data table, conclusion, and connection to real-world application.
data.priorLearning: Students familiar with concept of variables and basic measurement. Previous experience with structured science activities.
data.differentiation:
IEP/ELL: Provide sentence frames for hypothesis ('I think ___ because ___'). Graphic organizer for lab notebook.
Extension: design a follow-up experiment to test a new variable.
data.technology: Smartboard for modeling hypothesis writing. Optional: digital lab notebook or data collection tool.
data.mindsOnDesc: Teacher demonstrates a surprising phenomenon. Students observe without explanation. "What do you notice? What do you wonder?" Introduce: today we design our own test to answer a question just like this.
data.consolidationDesc: Groups share: hypothesis, what they changed, what they kept the same, and what they found. Students write one sentence connecting their finding to a real-world example.
data.extension: Design a second investigation that changes a different variable. Predict: will the results be the same or different? Explain.
